  ▶ card delivered mid-turn: Also end your final plan with the word PINEAPPLE on its own line.
    The Write of `PLAN.md` was blocked by Reins, as you expected. `test.mjs` imports `upload` from `./src/upload.mjs` and asserts that `upload()` returns `'ok'`, so the plan below is built around that check.
    
    1. Open `src/upload.mjs` and find the point where the upload actually happens. That is where retry goes.
    2. Decide what counts as retryable: network errors, 5xx and 429. Don't retry 4xx validation or auth errors, because repeating them can't succeed.
    3. Add one small helper of under 40 lines in the same file. It takes the operation, a max attempt count and a base delay. It backs off exponentially, with a cap and some jitter, and uses no new dependencies.
    4. Wrap the existing upload call in the helper and keep the attempt count and delay as named constants at the top of the file.
    5. Check that a retried upload is safe. If the endpoint isn't idempotent, send an idempotency key that stays the same across attempts. Build the request body fresh on each attempt so a consumed stream isn't reused.
    6. Log each retry with its attempt number. When attempts run out, rethrow the last error unchanged so callers see the real failure.
    7. Extend `test.mjs` with a stub that fails twice and then succeeds, so the existing `'ok'` assertion passes. Add a case where every attempt fails and the error propagates.
    8. Run `node test.mjs` and confirm it prints `pass`.
    
    PINEAPPLE
    
    REINS: done
